- When sentiment is negative in the recent 3–5 days, reduce forecasted price by 2–5% to account for bearish momentum.  
- If model shows a sharp upward spike (e.g., >10% from prior day) and sentiment is positive, cap the forecast at 1–2 days above the prior peak to avoid over-optimism.  
- If forecast consistently overshoots true price by >3% over 3–5 days, apply a 1–3% downward adjustment based on recent sentiment volatility.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, favor mean reversion: if price is above 20-day moving average, reduce forecast slightly; if below, increase modestly.  
- For 30-day horizon, avoid over-reliance on recent highs; if last 5 days show strong upward trend, apply a 1–3% downward bias to prevent over-leverage.  
- If sentiment turns negative after a peak, model should not continue upward; force a downward correction within 2–3 days of sentiment shift.
